messages:
anna-support: Hey team, customer on acct redwood-acme reports production API requests started returning 401 this morning after they ran a secrets sync. Response body: `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"API key not recognized\"}`. They say the same key worked earlier today.
maya: Do we have their request sample? ask them to paste the exact header (redact key).
anna-support: They pasted this curl: ```curl -i -H 'Authorization: Api-Key abc123def456ghi789:' https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat``` — note the scheme `Api-Key` and the key ends with a colon. Customer pasted from their Vault YAML where the secret value was stored as `|\n  abc123def456ghi789:` (literal block) — they think the trailing `:` came from a comment on the secret entry.
jordan: Hmm two things: `Api-Key` scheme is not the documented header — we expect `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (or `x-api-key` in older clients). The trailing colon would also mutate the key. Either could cause `invalid_api_key`.
ops-oncall: Quick repro: I tried the header exactly as pasted (masked) and got 401 with invalid_api_key. Tried same key without the trailing `:` — works. Also tried `Authorization: Api-Key` vs `Bearer` with same token: provider rejects `Api-Key` scheme too. So root cause looks like malformed header (scheme + colon suffix).
anna-support: Customer insists their rotation script copies straight from Vault via `vault read -format=json secret/keys/prod | jq -r .data.value` but they had YAML multiline in the secret value. They think the UI copy button included the trailing colon when they annotated the YAML.
maya: Can we offer a short remediation and a long-term? Immediate: ask them to re-copy the plain key (no punctuation), rotate the old key if it was exposed, and confirm requests succeed with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Long-term: recommend trimming punctuation if using the dashboard copy button and add checks in rotation script to `tr -d '[:space:]'` and `sed 's/:$//'` on the secret.
support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-14292. Attached request samples, mask applied. Notifying eng-runtime for possible UX edge-case in copy widget.
eng-runtime: assigning to @jordan to investigate copy behavior. Quick question: do we need server-side tolerance for stray punctuation in keys or is that unsafe (could mask real leaks)?
jordan: We should not accept modified keys server-side. Permit only exact match. Accepting punctuation would hide truncated/garbled secrets. UX fix only. I'll look into dashboard copy widget and Vault import pipeline.
ops-oncall: Customer confirmed after removing the trailing `:` and switching scheme to `Bearer` their requests are green. They rotated the exposed key and validated traffic.
anna-support: Marking customer as resolved, steps documented in ticket. Recommended checklist sent to customer: 1) rotate if exposed, 2) use `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, 3) trim punctuation from secret store values, 4) verify copy-paste from dashboard.
maya: Nice, also suggested they add a short unit test in their rotation script to call `GET /v1/usage` with the new key post-rotation.
anna-support: closing thread — thanks all :thumbsup:
